name: More Island Events
description: Adds new island events, written by the owner, to the ones the game draws from (more come in later versions). Five here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they join another tribe. The event is rare and separate: it never takes a share of the game's own draw (the stock island events' chances never change); after a natural island event, Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll may bring one of these events (or an Isola Grand Event Collection event) between two natural ones, never in trouble and never in place of a rescue, and Pick Island Event can pick it; it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not the Tribal Chief, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (200 to 600 food for the meat, 1,000 to 2,000 tech points for the chest) times the game's own multiplier for its events (the villagers it counts, divided by 20, plus 1). Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next) -- with Scrolling Popups installed, one scrolling popup for the question and one for each answer's result; the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Troubling Signs (The Secret City only): the Tribal Chief, wearing the chief's robe, asks one of four groups for advice in a popup with four buttons (the game's own look; the mouse, or the keys 1 to 4): the spiritual leaders (the village loses food), the magicians (gains tech points), the naturalists (gains food) or the scientists and healers (loses tech points) -- a random amount as the Aspiring Adventurer's, 200 to 600 food or 1,000 to 2,000 tech points, times the game's own multiplier; a loss never takes more than is stored. Each group's advisor speaks, the chief calls the tribe by its own name, and the decree sends five villagers of 18 or more away for good (no graves). It needs the robed chief, nine other villagers of 18 or more who are not nursing a baby (four advisors, who stay, and the five) and a population of 61 or more (The Lost Children's "A Dangerous Mission" rule: the living villagers plus the babies being carried); it never takes a share of the game's own draw: it comes through Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll or Pick Island Event. And Diving for Treasure (The Secret City only): a villager of 18 or more dives for something shimmering on the reef. "Swim deeper": 1 in 4 each, golden doubloons (tech points), a useless buoy, a container of exotic ingredients (food) -- a random amount as the Aspiring Adventurer's, 1,000 to 2,000 tech points or 200 to 600 food, times the game's own multiplier -- or an air tank pops: 75% the diver gets ashore and now dislikes swimming; 25% the diver sinks: dies (17%, a grave), is never found (17%, no grave) or is rescued (66%, +10 to 20 Healing, at most 100). "Better not": +10 to 20 Parenting, at most 100. It needs two villagers of 18 or more who are not nursing a baby and not the Tribal Chief (the diver, and another named as the head Doctor on the rescue page); it never takes a share of the game's own draw: it comes through Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll or Pick Island Event. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave: everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone -- each at the graveyard, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each), and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished structure: an earthquake damages each of the three population huts and the clothing hut one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each can come again. Pick Island Event lists each of these events and picks one whenever its own requirements hold (otherwise it says what the event needs). Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs Story / Cheat Upgrades (on by default), which runs the rare roll and Pick Island Event; ticking this ticks it.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.
behavior_changes: The event is rare and separate: it never takes a share of the game's own draw (the stock island events' chances never change); after a natural island event, Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll may bring one of these events (or an Isola Grand Event Collection event) between two natural ones, never in trouble and never in place of a rescue, and Pick Island Event can pick it. It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not the Tribal Chief; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer.

Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 200 to 600 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 1,000 to 2,000 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half.

Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), joins another tribe (gone for good, no grave), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears.

The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer, times the game's own multiplier for its events (the villagers it counts, divided by 20, plus 1). The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one.

The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK.

The Troubling Signs (The Secret City): needs the Tribal Chief in the robe (+0xE80 and the robe's body +0xDF4 = 29, as the robing 0x45FBC0 writes them), nine other different villagers of 18 or more (360 age units) who are not protected (adv_is_protected: nursing +0xE8C, the chief +0xE80) -- four advisors (one per group, the same four for the event; they stay) and five travellers, any nine equally likely -- a population of 61 or more (The Lost Children's 0x425860 rule: the living villagers plus the babies carried, litter +0xE90) and the tribe's name (the game object [0x4B309C] +0x12ED4). It shares table slot 0 with The Aspiring Adventurer and Diving for Treasure and never takes a share of the draw: the loop-end stub adds no entry to the selector's list and puts the object of the event that is due (Story / Cheat Upgrades' rare roll or Pick Island Event) in slot 0, which Story / Cheat Upgrades' pick then presents in place of the stock event drawn. The popup is the game's own dialog 0x4192F0 with two more answer buttons made as its constructor makes its two (0x46EC93, picture 4 via 0x42E9D0 / 0x42E8A0, 0x4019F0 ids 4 and 5, labels 0x4185A0 / 0x401620, add-child 0x40C1F0), stacked and centred 1.5 button heights apart, room for them measured by the game's own paragraph 0x40A0C0; that dialog's virtual table is a copy of 0x47F28C with its own click (ids 4 and 5) and key handlers (Enter / Esc OK, 1-4 the answers); Scrolling Popups' reserve adds VvfpMoreIslandEventsButtonRoom. Each answer's award is a normal one (the game's range, then its multiplier); the effects -- the five removed as a living villager is (no body), told to Cause of Death, and the award through the game's own writer (a loss at most what is stored) -- are made when the decree's last page is shown, with the event's one Island Events log entry. No site of its own.

Diving for Treasure (The Secret City): the diver and the rescue page's head Doctor are two different villagers of 18 or more (360 age units) who may be picked (vv3_eligible: alive +0xE78, present +0xF10, not a look-alike +0xE94, adv_is_protected: nursing +0xE8C, the chief +0xE80), each drawn among them. One more two-choice object with the Adventurer's virtual table and methods (adv_flow), put in slot 0 only while it is due (t_list adds no entry to the selector's list). "Swim deeper": rand(4) A / B / C / D; D: rand(100) < 75 survives -- swimming (preference 37 of the game's list at file 0x97488) taken from the likes +0xFB4 and added to the dislikes +0xFC0 -- else sinks: rand(100) < 17 the game's own death (0x462670, health 0, cause -1: a grave), < 34 removed as a living villager is (no body; told to Cause of Death), else +10 to 20 Healing (+0xEB4); A a normal tech award, C a normal food award (the game's range, then its multiplier, through 0x427130 / 0x4263F0). "Better not": +10 to 20 Parenting (+0xEB0). Skills at most 100 (the game's own adder 0x455740 caps at 0x64). The effects are made when the ending's last page is shown, with the event's one Island Events log entry. No site of its own.

The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each in slot 0 only while it is due (t_list adds no entry), no site of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the graveyard, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each); the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the three population huts and the clothing hut finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state); the building's effect handle freed and set to -1.
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist.
Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.
evidence_status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the draw, the popup pages, both choices' effects and the install with every other patch emulated on the stock executable in tests/test_aspiring_adventurer.py (The Troubling Signs: who, the draw, all four answers by mouse and key, the effects on the last page, the log entry, the words and the four buttons, in tests/test_troubling_signs.py; Diving for Treasure: who, every branch at its odds, every effect on the last page, the log entry, the words and the draw with 1, 2 and 3 events, in tests/test_diving_for_treasure.py); The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings: the conditions, the draw, everyone sent and where, the feast, the damage and its states, the log entry and the words, in tests/test_ceremony_and_rumblings.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
